🌎 BEYOND THE 956

John Anderson, the Country Music Hall of Fame member whose unmistakable vocal twang carried '70s, '80s and '90s hits like "Swingin'," "Wild and Blue" and "Seminole Wind," has died at 71.

Anderson's family announced his death Wednesday, October 21, 2026, in a statement shared on his official social media accounts. He died peacefully in his sleep at his home in Smithville, Tennessee, his family said. A cause of death was not disclosed.

"It is with the heaviest of hearts that we share the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and best friend," the family wrote. "To the world, he was a gifted country music singer whose voice and songs touched countless lives. To us, he was so much more."

A native of Apopka, Florida, Anderson moved to Nashville in 1971 to chase a recording career, working odd jobs — including helping put the roof on the new Grand Ole Opry House — before his first hit, "I've Got a Feelin' (Somebody's Been Stealin')," broke through in 1977. He went on to release more than 20 albums and rack up five No. 1 singles on the country chart.

Alongside artists like George Strait and Ricky Skaggs, Anderson was counted as one of the "New Traditionalists" who carried classic country into the modern era. His biggest hit, "Swingin'," was named Single of the Year by the Country Music Association in 1983, and he was inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2014 and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2024.

Just days before his death, Anderson appeared in public at the Hall of Fame's Medallion Ceremony on Sunday, October 18, where Tim McGraw, Paul Overstreet and the Stanley Brothers were inducted. McGraw wrote on Instagram that he was "completely heartbroken" and that Anderson had been "in such good spirits" that night.

"John Anderson was a one-of-a-kind song stylist," said Kyle Young, CEO of the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. "He was already a diamond then, and a diamond he always will be."

He is survived by his wife, Jamie, two daughters and grandchildren.

Sources: statement from John Anderson's family via his official social media; The Associated Press; USA Today; Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum.
